name: connectwise-automate
description: ConnectWise Automate (RMM): computers and their software, services, drives, patching, alerts and history; clients, scripts and commands; gated script runs, commands and reboots; interactive fleet, client and computer views.
long_description:
ConnectWise Automate (RMM) as a local MCP server. Search computers and read each one's software, services, drives, patch compliance, hardware, monitors, alerts, script history and command history; list clients, locations, contacts, groups, scripts, schedules, running scripts, alerts, monitors, commands, tickets, users, patch history and network devices; and reach anything else through cw_automate_api_get (GET only).

Every tool is named cw_automate_* and shows a Title Case name in the client. Read tools carry readOnlyHint. The interactive views (cw_automate_view_fleet, cw_automate_view_computers, cw_automate_view_computer, cw_automate_view_client) render as MCP Apps cards; the computer view has Run script and Reboot buttons that call the gated write tools.

WRITES ARE GATED. Running a script, queuing a command or shell command, and updating a client or location stay listed but refuse until you turn on Automate write mode. Reboots, disruptive agent commands, script-schedule deletes, uninstalls and cw_automate_api_write are the disruptive tier and also need Automate allow destructive. Every write call carries confirm: true. cw_status_gate explains a refusal.

This bundle runs on your own machine and holds the Automate credentials there. PSA ships as a separate bundle from the same repository.

automate_password.title: Automate password
automate_password.description: Automate account password. Supply it from your secret manager.

automate_client_id.title: Automate clientId
automate_client_id.description: Automate developer clientId GUID, sent with every Automate request.

automate_totp_secret.title: Automate TOTP secret
automate_totp_secret.description: Only needed when the Automate login account keeps two-factor authentication enabled. Paste the same base32 seed the account's authenticator was enrolled with and the connector generates each passcode itself. The cleaner alternative is a dedicated API service account exempt from two-factor; leave this blank then.

automate_write_mode.title: Automate write mode
automate_write_mode.description: Allow the Automate write tools (run a script, queue an agent command or shell command, update a client or location) to act on live machines. Off by default: write tools stay listed and refuse with a message naming this switch. Every write call also needs confirm: true.

automate_allow_destructive.title: Automate allow destructive
automate_allow_destructive.description: Also allow the disruptive Automate tier: reboots, disruptive agent commands (shutdown, service stop, logoff…), script-schedule deletes, software uninstalls and the raw cw_automate_api_write passthrough. Needs Automate write mode on as well.
